views.reconstructed_statement: For every nonnegative integer degree d, every infinite real coefficient sequence c, and every real u,v,lo,hi, assume 0<=u<v<=1 and lo<=c(r)<=hi for each integer r with 0<=r<=d. Then for every integer i with 0<=i<=d, the coefficient R(i) obtained by the following two subdivisions lies in the same closed interval [lo,hi]. Write D_t(c)(j)=(1-t)c(j)+t c(j+1); casteljau(m,c,t,j) means D_t iterated m times and evaluated at j. Set L_t(c)(i)=D_t^i(c)(0), set Q(i)=L_(1-u)(r -> c(d-r))(d-i), using natural subtraction max(d-i,0), and set R(i)=L_s(Q)(i), where s=(v-u)/(1-u). These are exact real equalities, with no rounding or tolerance. Equivalently Q(i)=sum over j=0,...,max(d-i,0) of c(d-j) B(max(d-i,0),j,1-u); for i<=d all accessed original indices are between i and d. For i>d, Q(i)=c(d), explaining why the supplied right-restriction node legitimately quantifies over all natural i. The root itself quantifies only over i<=d. The assumptions imply u<1, so the denominator 1-u is strictly positive and s belongs to (0,1]. The asserted range preservation is a closed-interval coefficient bound, not a statement about normalized quantum amplitudes.

domains_and_quantifiers.c: all functions Nat -> Real; no finite-support requirement

hypotheses: for every natural r<=d, lo<=c(r) and c(r)<=hi
semantic_slots.closed_interval_meaning: membership in Set.Icc lo hi means the conjunction lo<=value and value<=hi
semantic_slots.basis: B(d,r,t)=binomial(d,r)t^r(1-t)^(d-r), with natural subtraction and binomial(d,r)=0 when r>d; only r<=d occurs in the finite sums used here
semantic_slots.normalization: Bernstein weights sum to one for every real t; they are nonnegative on [0,1]. This is affine weight normalization only.
boundary_cases: d=0: the sole admitted coefficient and the output R(0) both equal c(0).
u=0 and v=1 are admitted jointly; u=v and u=1 are excluded.
v=1 gives s=1 and remains admitted.
No lo<=hi premise is written separately. The coefficient premise implies it through c(0); if lo>hi the implication has no satisfying coefficient premise.
There is no empty degree-d coefficient range: it always contains index zero. Coefficients beyond d have no effect on the claimed output indices.

obligation_nodes.meaning: For every d>=0 and every real t, sum_(r=0)^d B(d,r,t)=1; no restriction t in [0,1] is needed for this identity.
For every d,c,t,lo,hi, if 0<=t<=1 and all first d+1 coefficients lie in [lo,hi], their Bernstein-weighted sum lies in [lo,hi]. Both premises are required.
For every d,c,u,lo,hi, if 0<=u<=1 and all first d+1 coefficients lie in [lo,hi], then Q(i) lies there for every natural i, including i>d via truncated subtraction.
For all real u,v satisfying all three inequalities 0<=u, u<v, v<=1, the exact-real quotient (v-u)/(1-u) belongs to [0,1].
Under every original premise, all admitted restricted coefficients belong to the same interval.

semantic_slots.registers_phase_oracles_resources: No register, basis-state phase, oracle, state preparation, success probability, runtime, gate-count, or bit-complexity object occurs in the target.
semantic_slots.exact_asserted_scope: A conditional exact-real range-preservation proposition over every natural degree and all admissible data; no checked Lean execution is reported by this decoder.

ambiguities: The literal casteljauStep declaration is not included, but its row-update equation and the casteljau_eq_sum interface are supplied, so the needed mathematical update is identifiable.
The packet supplies signatures and definitions, not proof terms or an independent compilation result.
dependency_audit: sp110_partition alone is insufficient for sp110_convex: a sum of weights equal to one need not be nonnegative. The separately supplied basis_nonneg interface and the interval premise are essential. For example, d=1,c(0)=0,c(1)=1,t=2 has sum of weights one but weighted value 2.

The stated graph edges are not exhaustive standalone implications. Connecting convex sums to rightRestriction/root also uses the casteljau_eq_sum interface, definitions, and bounds on the natural indices.
sp110_right does not need an added i<=d premise: natural subtraction saturates, giving c(d) beyond d. Treating d-i as signed subtraction would invalidate that reading.
limitations: The root does not assert a polynomial identity for the reparameterized function, even though its coefficient construction is the supplied de Casteljau construction.
It supplies no approximation error, positive lower bound, finite-bit algorithm, resource estimate, normalized state, circuit, or optimality claim.
No claim of equivalence to an external source question, human approval, proof-body audit, or current Lean certification is made.
